tasks.title: Ship 3 librarian agents + MCP servers: self-updating project indexes, selectable in /init-team, wired to the lanes that consult them
notes: USER: deferred by request ('later once you finish'). Queued behind T8.

REFERENCE PATTERN (read from '/home/ubuntu/source/Appnext Campaign AI/campaign-ai-platform/.claude/agents'): _librarian-template.md (canonical, 190 lines), history-librarian.md, tests-librarian.md, compliance-officer.md (55KB). Shape of each: haiku model; tools Glob/Grep/Read/Bash/Write/Edit; owns a private memory dir .claude/agent-memory/<name>/ holding an append-only commits.jsonl plus rolling summary_overall.md and summary_by_file.md; SELF-UPDATES incrementally on every invocation (e.g. git log since the last indexed hash); answers FROM memory via a bash search helper so the caller never pays for raw git output; explicitly does not touch production code, bump versions or push. Descriptions carry 2-3 <example> blocks so the orchestrator auto-delegates. Librarians consult each other (compliance-officer consults tests-librarian).
GOAL: teamme maps the project once via librarians instead of every generated agent re-deriving the same map its own way. The librarians are the project-comprehension layer, not roster filler.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS for the future brief: (1) 'gate' needs defining - MCP tool-level refusal like teamme_install (precedent now exists in T8) vs a hook, which invariant #1 forbids from blocking; (2) 'self-updated autonomously with hooks' needs a trigger that cannot loop (invariant #2) and cannot block (invariant #1) - SessionStart is the safe candidate, PostToolUse is not; (3) which 3 - the reference set is git-history, tests-coverage and compliance, but teamme's own layer boundaries may imply different ones; (4) a librarian's memory is per-project state: committed or gitignored? (5) invariant #4 - librarian prompts are project-agnostic templates, their INDEXES are project-specific.

HISTORY-LIBRARIAN SCOPE (user, for the future brief): go beyond answering 'what changed in file X'. Two capabilities: (1) build a codebase MAP from historical changes read chronologically - the commit stream is the evidence, so structure emerges from how the code actually evolved rather than from a one-off static scan; (2) print a COMPLETE DEPENDENCY TREE of anything - workflow -> references -> scopes -> features -> tests, with the tests leg answered by consulting the tests-librarian rather than re-deriving it. That cross-librarian consultation is the pattern already present in the reference implementation (compliance-officer consults tests-librarian) and is what makes the map cheap: each librarian owns one axis and is asked, never re-computed.

tasks.title: Add /queue: park a request as a work-log task with a one-line ack, no grounding, no brief, no analysis
notes: WHY: /intake on a parked request still burns a full grounding+analysis response (see T14). /queue should be the cheap path: record it, print the task id, stop.

DESIGN NOTES: (1) thin wrapper over 'worklog.py add' with optional --priority; output is ONE line - the task id and title, nothing else. (2) Must be added to route-to-intake.py PASSTHROUGH or the hook will nag the user to run /intake on their own /queue call - same class of bug as T6. (3) Works regardless of phase: idle, grounding or approved - parking never touches intake-state. (4) /intake step 0's existing 'Queue' triage row is the same action taken autonomously; /queue exposes it to the user directly. Keep the two consistent. (5) Consider the inverse later: a command to pull a parked task INTO intake ('worklog.py next' already finds it).

REFINEMENT: /intake must short-circuit to the /queue path itself when the request signals deferral ('later', 'once you finish', 'after X', 'queue this'), instead of grounding it. Two distinct gaps: (1) step 0's Queue row only applies when an intake is ALREADY in flight - a deferral arriving at an idle phase still falls through to 0b and gets full grounding; the deferral test must run BEFORE the phase check. (2) The Queue row says 'tell the user the task id' but caps nothing, so the response stays long - see T14, correctly queued and still answered with paragraphs. The queue path must specify a ONE-LINE response as a hard output constraint, in both /queue and /intake's Queue row.

Prompt lane landed and verified by me: queue.md has valid frontmatter with a hard one-line output contract; intake.md gained step 0a (deferral test ahead of the phase check) and the Queue row now caps the response; all six placeholders intact; the only intake-state reference inside 0a is the prohibition itself. validate.sh passes. Blocked on the router passthrough before it is actually cheap.

preflight misdiagnoses every existing 0.1.0 install as not-installed and tells the user to run /init-team over a working team
notes: Reproduced against /home/ubuntu/source/speedrun-nanosuit, a real 0.1.0 install: hook registration PASSES (all 4 events) and intake command PASSES, yet state reports not-installed, because 'hook scripts' fails on the newly-added preflight.py and liveness reports 'never' (0.1.0 settings never wired the heartbeat). Needs a fourth state - installed-outdated - whose remediation is a repair (teamme_install / team-doctor), never /init-team. This is the upgrade path every existing user will hit.

GROUNDED. Root cause: preflight.py:335 scaffolded = hooks.ok AND settings.ok; _check_hooks fails if ANY name in REQUIRED_HOOKS is absent, and preflight.py was added to that tuple in 0.2.0. Structural: every future release adding a hook retroactively marks all existing installs not-installed. Grounding also found four consumers the plan missed: queue.md:52-55 infers install state independently and hard-codes init-team; the CLI exits on ok not state, and intake.md:38 halts on non-zero, so an outdated install will halt /intake until repaired; teamme_mcp.py:353 ties teamme_install to the literal not-installed; teamme_mcp.py:234 globs *.py while REQUIRED_HOOKS is a separate list that can drift.

preflight: 'installed' now derives from install evidence (registered teamme hooks / generated intake.md), not the growing REQUIRED_HOOKS list; added the installed-outdated state with repair-only remediation, a third liveness branch, and a REPAIR_FIX swap in diagnose(). MCP: teamme_status/teamme_install advise repair on installed-outdated, and install audits templates/hooks against REQUIRED_HOOKS. Pipe-tested against the real 0.1.0 install (speedrun-nanosuit) plus synthetic 0.1.0/empty/full/heartbeat/malformed cases; validate.sh passes; .claude/hooks copies re-synced.

Extended scripts/validate.sh with 4 new preflight assertions covering the installed vs complete regression: (1) a synthetic 0.1.0-shaped fixture (5 original hooks, no preflight.py, settings.json missing the heartbeat entry) asserts state==installed-outdated, non-zero exit, and no fix text containing init-team; (2) full scaffolding pre-heartbeat now explicitly asserts installed-not-live before the existing live-baseline check; (3) a stranger's repo with an unrelated SessionStart hook and no teamme scaffolding asserts state==not-installed (false-positive guard on _install_evidence); (4) a JSON-RPC-driven teamme_install call against the outdated fixture asserts the repaired state becomes installed-not-live (never installed-outdated) and that .claude/commands/intake.md content is byte-identical before/after. Each new assertion was observed failing (reverting installed=complete flips the fixture back to not-installed with init-team in the fix text; forcing liveness true breaks assertion 2; broadening the evidence probe match breaks assertion 3; simulating an intake.md overwrite in install() breaks assertion 4) and then restored to passing. ./scripts/validate.sh prints ALL CHECKS PASSED.

Folded P0 install-state fix into 0.2.0 (unreleased): CHANGELOG date updated to 2026-09-24, entry corrected from three install states to four (not-installed, installed-outdated, installed-not-live, live), evidence-based existence checking explained. plugin.json and CHANGELOG now agree on v0.2.0. validate.sh passes.

ALL LANES LANDED, verified by me: speedrun-nanosuit (a real 0.1.0 install) now reports installed-outdated with zero init-team mentions; four new validate.sh assertion groups pass, each watched failing first; docs corrected in 4 files with Known gaps growing 7->8; changelog re-dated 2026-09-24 with the false three-states claim removed.
